name: Hadlai
title: Father of Amasa from the tribe of Ephraim
summary: Hadlai is a person mentioned in 2 Chronicles as the father of Amasa, one of the leaders of the tribe of Ephraim. He is mentioned in connection with the event where the leaders of Ephraim persuaded the Israelite soldiers to release the captives from Judah who had been taken during King Pekah's war against King Ahaz.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as father of Amasa
keyEvents.description: Hadlai is mentioned as the father of Amasa, one of the heads of the tribe of Ephraim who received the prophet Oded's warning.

keyEvents.title: The leaders of Ephraim intervene
keyEvents.description: Hadlai's son Amasa was among the leaders who opposed taking the captives from Judah into Samaria and demanded that they be set free.

keyEvents.title: The captives are released and helped
keyEvents.description: As a result of the efforts of the leaders, including Hadlai's son, the captives were clothed, given food and drink, and sent back to Jericho.

keyEvents.title: The Prophet Oded's Warning
keyEvents.description: The prophet Oded warned the army of Israel that their victory over Judah was due to God's anger, but that they had gone too far in their cruelty—this was the background for Hadlai's son and other leaders intervening.
